intervention_dose: HA-1 TCR-transduced CD8+ and CD4+ T cells with a CD8 coreceptor, given after lymphodepletion; one or more infusions
population_detail: Recurrent AML/ALL/MDS/JMML after allo-HCT; HLA-A*02:01-positive with recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch. n=9 treated.

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: achieved or maintained CR after lymphodepletion + HA-1 TCR-T; trial not powered for efficacy; 1 patient in remission >2y

safety_summary: No dose-limiting toxicities, no CRS and no ICANS across 9 patients. The main events were brief self-resolving fever, grade 3-4 neutropenia and grade 3-5 infections from lymphodepletion, and two cases of mild grade 1-2 acute GVHD tied to withdrawal of immunosuppression rather than the TCR-T.

toxicities.notes: grade 2 GI and grade 1 skin; attributed to immunosuppression withdrawal, not TCR-T
included Legionella and S. aureus pneumonia

notes: Per-term AE detail pulled from PMC full text (PMC11406181); the Blood abstract reported only 'no DLTs'. Closest published precedent for the patient's primary HA-1 handle (NCT03326921); commercial HA-1/HA-2 programs TSC-100/101 and BSB-1001 have no published clinical results yet.

intervention_dose: Donor-derived WT1-specific TCRC4 transduced into EBV-specific central-memory CD8+ T cells; infused prophylactically post-HCT
population_detail: HLA-A*02:01-positive, WT1-positive high-risk AML given as post-HCT relapse prophylaxis; compared with a concurrent 88-patient similar-risk cohort.
design: Phase 1/2 single-arm with concurrent comparator cohort
safety_summary: The product was built on EBV-specific CD8+ T cells to limit GVHD risk; the report emphasized persistence and polyfunctionality without a treatment-limiting toxicity signal. No per-term AE table in the abstract.

toxicities.notes: TCRC4 delivered on EBV-specific CD8+ Tcm to minimize GVHD; no treatment-limiting GVHD signal reported in abstract

notes: Anchors the WT1 A*02:01 TCR-T arm; a prophylaxis product since succeeded by FH-WT1-E50, so precedent rather than an open slot. Abstract carries no AE table; full text (PMC6982533) would be needed for per-term safety.

intervention_dose: WT1-specific siTCR-transduced lymphocytes, two transfers 4 weeks apart in a dose-escalation design, followed by sequential WT1 peptide vaccines
population_detail: HLA-A*24:02-positive, WT1-positive refractory AML and high-risk MDS; two dose cohorts, n=8.
outcome: Transient marrow blast reduction; T-cell persistence

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: transient decrease in marrow blasts, associated with hematopoietic recovery

outcomes.name: OS_rate
outcomes.notes: 4 of 5 patients with persistent T cells at study end survived >12 months

safety_summary: No adverse events attributable to normal tissue across the 8 patients; TCR-T cells persisted in 5 of 8 and retained WT1-specific reactivity.

toxicities.notes: no adverse events of normal tissue reported

notes: The A*24:02-restricted WT1-siTCR fallback lever if the patient types HLA-A*02:01-negative. Small early-phase Japanese cohort; abstract reports no per-term AE table beyond the absence of normal-tissue toxicity.

intervention_label: Multiantigen leukemia-specific donor T cells (mLST; PRAME/WT1/Survivin/NY-ESO-1)
intervention_dose: Donor-derived T cells reactive to PRAME, WT1, Survivin and NY-ESO-1; escalating doses 0.5 to 10 ×10^7 cells/m2
population_detail: Post-HCT AML/MDS; 17 at high risk of relapse (prophylaxis) and 8 with active disease; products generated from 29 donors, 25 patients infused.
median_dor_or_pfs: median leukemia-free and overall survival not reached at 1.9 y

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.notes: median OS not reached at 1.9y follow-up

safety_summary: Infusions were well tolerated with no grade >2 acute GVHD and no extensive chronic GVHD across the 25 recipients.
notes: Published precedent for the multiantigen PRAME/WT1/Survivin donor T-cell approach in AML/MDS (NCT02494167), the same mechanism as the trials.jsonl TAA-T row; WT1 and PRAME expression on the patient's blasts should be confirmed.

intervention_dose: 12 µg/kg IV on days 1-5 of each 21-day cycle
population_detail: CD123+ BPDCN; 29 previously untreated at 12 µg/kg (primary-outcome cohort) plus 15 previously treated. Not the patient's disease.
safety_summary: Capillary leak syndrome occurred in 19% and was linked to one death in each dose subgroup; hepatic transaminase elevation and thrombocytopenia were common.

toxicities.notes: associated with one death in each dose subgroup

notes: Registration study behind the CD123-directed BPDCN approval; carries the mechanism and off-label precedent for the patient's CD123 handle, but BPDCN is not AML so this is cross-tumor read-across. Capillary-leak and hepatic risk are relevant given the undocumented organ function.

intervention_dose: 0.045 mg/kg IV once every 3 weeks (recommended phase 2 dose)
population_detail: CD123+ R/R AML, ECOG 0-1; first-in-human dose-escalation/expansion, RP2D expansion cohort n=29 (whole study n=91).
safety_summary: At the RP2D the most common grade 3+ treatment-related events were febrile neutropenia (10%), infusion-related reactions (7%) and anaemia (7%); dose-limiting reversible veno-occlusive disease and neutropenia were seen at higher doses, with one treatment-related death across schedule A.

toxicities.notes: dose-limiting, reversible; at 0.180 and 0.450 mg/kg (schedule A)

notes: Single-agent CD123 ADC activity in R/R AML matching the patient's CD123 positivity; quantitative antigen density (advisory) is still pending. VOD signal is notable given the planned second transplant.

intervention_dose: 500 ng/kg per day continuous infusion (RP2D), with week-1 step-up dosing, pretreatment dexamethasone and tocilizumab as needed
indication: Primary induction failure / early-relapse R/R AML
population_detail: Primary induction failure or early relapse (<6 mo) R/R AML; benefit enriched in an immune-infiltrated tumor microenvironment. RP2D PIF/ER subset n=30 (whole study n=88).
median_dor_or_pfs: median OS 10.2 mo among CR/CRh responders
safety_summary: Infusion-related reactions and cytokine release syndrome were the most frequent events, largely grade 1-2; step-up dosing, pretreatment dexamethasone and prompt tocilizumab prevented severe IRR/CRS.

toxicities.notes: most frequent AE, largely grade 1-2; mitigated with step-up dosing, dexamethasone, tocilizumab
severe events largely prevented per authors; granular per-term grade-3 rates are in the full text / CT.gov AE tab (NCT02152956)

notes: Efficacy precedent for CD123xCD3 bispecific salvage in chemo-refractory AML close to the patient's state; MacroGenics has since deprioritized the program, so it is mechanism evidence rather than an open route. Abstract gives no per-term grade-3 CRS rate; CT.gov NCT02152956 AE tab holds the breakdown.

intervention_dose: 9 mg/m2 IV over 2 hours, 2 doses 14 days apart (monotherapy)
indication: CD33+ AML in untreated first relapse
population_detail: CD33+ AML in untreated first relapse, no antecedent hematologic disorder; median age 61. Pooled across three open-label trials.

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: overall remission with monotherapy in first relapse

safety_summary: Grade 3/4 hyperbilirubinemia in 23% and transaminase elevation in 17%, with low rates of grade 3/4 mucositis (4%); veno-occlusive disease is the characteristic class risk. No treatment-related cardiotoxicity.
notes: On-label CD33 ADC monotherapy in first relapse; single-agent depth is modest (30%) and the patient is further along with FLAG-IDA/venetoclax failure and extramedullary disease. Hepatic/VOD risk matters ahead of a second transplant.

intervention_label: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin added to induction chemotherapy (ALFA-0701)
intervention_dose: 3 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 4, 7 of induction and day 1 of each of two consolidations (fractionated), added to standard chemotherapy
population_detail: Previously untreated de novo AML age 50-70 (excludes APL); CD33 expression not required for entry. 280 randomized.
comparator: Standard induction chemotherapy without gemtuzumab ozogamicin
safety_summary: Persistent thrombocytopenia was more frequent with gemtuzumab ozogamicin (16% vs 3%) without an increase in death from toxicity; veno-occlusive disease is the characteristic class risk.
notes: Pivotal RCT behind the fractionated-dose gemtuzumab schedule; front-line de novo add-on, so line and setting differ from this R/R patient. Benefit was concentrated in favourable/intermediate cytogenetics.

intervention_label: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin added to induction (IPD meta-analysis)
intervention_dose: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (3 or 6 mg/m2) added to first-course intensive induction across five RCTs
population_detail: 3325 adults with AML (excluding APL) in five randomized induction trials; cytogenetic risk subgroups analyzed, including an adverse-cytogenetics stratum.

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: no survival benefit (2.2% absolute) in the adverse-cytogenetics stratum

safety_summary: The 3 mg/m2 dose caused fewer early deaths than 6 mg/m2 at equal efficacy; per-term toxicity was not the focus of this individual-patient-data meta-analysis.

toxicities.notes: higher with 6 mg/m2 than 3 mg/m2 at equal efficacy; per-term AE breakdown not reported in this IPD meta-analysis

notes: Highest-tier CD33 evidence, and the decision-relevant point for this patient is the null adverse-cytogenetics subgroup (OR 0.99): patients with adverse karyotype derived no survival benefit, which directly tempers the CD33 handle here given the complex/TP53-aberrant karyotype.

intervention_dose: 131I-apamistamab anti-CD45 radioconjugate, individualized dosimetry-based activity, before allogeneic HCT
indication: Active relapsed/refractory AML, age >=55, planned allo-HCT
population_detail: Active R/R AML age >=55 fit for allo-HCT; ITT included crossover (52% of conventional-care arm received 131I-apamistamab). Enrolled patients heading to a first allo-HCT.

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: ITT; OS not improved, diluted by 52% crossover to RIT

safety_summary: Grade 3+ treatment-related adverse events occurred in 59.7% of the 131I-apamistamab group versus 59.2% with conventional care; the agent was well tolerated as pretransplant conditioning.

toxicities.notes: vs 59.2% conventional care; per-term breakdown on CT.gov AE tab (NCT02665065)

notes: Randomized evidence that CD45-targeted radioimmunotherapy can carry active R/R AML into allo-HCT, speaking to conditioning a second transplant with an 85%-blast marrow. SIERRA enrolled patients going to a first transplant, so prior-HCT eligibility is the axis to check. OS was flat because most control patients crossed over.

intervention_dose: Eprenetapopt 4.5 g/day IV days 1-4, venetoclax 400 mg/day days 1-28, azacitidine 75 mg/m2 days 1-7 (28-day cycles)
population_detail: Treatment-naive TP53-mutant AML with >=1 pathogenic TP53 mutation, ECOG 0-2; triplet expansion evaluable n=39 (whole study n=49). Pan-p53 reactivator, not Y220C-selective.
safety_summary: Grade 3+ events in >=20% were febrile neutropenia (47%), thrombocytopenia (37%), leukopenia (25%) and anaemia (22%); treatment-related serious AEs in 27% and one treatment-related death (sepsis).
notes: Eprenetapopt is a pan-p53 reactivator, not Y220C-selective, and the profile flags it low-yield; the front-line treatment-naive setting also differs from this R/R patient. Kept so the board can weigh the pan-reactivator track against the Y220C-selective rezatapopt option.

intervention_dose: Eprenetapopt 4.5 g/day IV days 1-4 + azacitidine 75 mg/m2 days 1-7 (28-day cycles)
population_detail: TP53-mutant MDS (n=40), oligoblastic AML with 20-30% blasts (n=11), and MDS/MPN (n=4); frontline. 35% went on to allo-HCT.

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.notes: median OS; responders 14.6 vs 7.5 mo by landmark, p=0.0005

safety_summary: Most common grade 3+ events were febrile neutropenia (33%), leukopenia (29%) and neutropenia (29%); the profile matched azacitidine or eprenetapopt monotherapy.
notes: The doublet phase 1b/2 in TP53-mutant MDS/oligoblastic AML; the subsequent randomized phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS did not meet its primary endpoint, and eprenetapopt is not Y220C-selective, reinforcing the low-yield framing for this patient.

exclusion_reason: No peer-reviewed clinical efficacy data to extract yet: the solid-tumor PYNNACLE study (NCT04585750) and the myeloid rezatapopt + azacitidine trial (NCT06616636) are ongoing with results limited to conference abstracts. Also Y220C-contingent, and the patient's TP53 status and specific variant are unresolved.
notes: The Y220C-selective reactivator is the actionable TP53 handle if a Y220C variant is confirmed; retained for the audit trail with no manuscript to source effect sizes or toxicities from.

exclusion_reason: Program discontinued, and the phase 1 optimized-dose study enrolled MRD-positive AML, which does not match the patient's overt high-burden relapse (~85% marrow blasts).
notes: CD123xCD3 bispecific in the same sub-pipeline as flotetuzumab; kept for landscape completeness but not an enrollment route.
